Man Explores Abandoned Property, Finds Rare Million-Dollar 1928 Bentley in a Barn
9 photos
Photo: The Bearded Explorer/YouTube
Most barn finds we see today are usually mundane classics that aren't worth saving. However, from time to time, barn find explorers stumble across rare and desirable vehicles. While some have six-figure potential, a few can actually morph into million-dollar rigs . The Bentley you're about to see below is one of those vehicles.
Found by Colin Smith of "The Bearded Explorer" YouTube channel, this classic Bentley is parked on what appears to be an abandoned property. Its exact location in the UK remains undisclosed, but it looks like it has been left behind a few good years ago. It's unclear what happened, but whoever owned this place also abandoned a few classic cars.
Most of the vehicles are quite common in places like this in Britain. The property is home to a couple of Reliant Scimitars. Built between 1964 and 1986, the Scimitar was born as a two-door coupe and morphed into a shooting brake in 1968. The company also added a convertible to the lineup in 1980.
Reliant produced about 15,400 units in total, but the Scimitar is largely unknown outside of Britain. It's also a relatively rare classic today, especially when it comes to examples in solid condition. And the interesting thing here is that one of the cars is a first-gen coupe.
Reliant built only 1,006 examples between 1964 and 1970, split between the SE4, SE4A, and SE4C (depending on the engine). All told, this car is one of a few hundred units produced, regardless of what's under the hood.
Our host also found an E21-spec BMW 3 Series parked outside, plus an old race car parked in a barn. The latter is a bit of a mystery, with no identification except for the Jaguar inline-six engine. It could be a custom-built racer, most likely for hillclimb events.
But the big highlight here is the 1928 Bentley stashed in one of the barns. The car hasn't been moved in years, but it appears to be in one piece. It's a 4 1/2 Litre model, which is one of Bentley's most famous creations.
The British company produced the 4 1/2 Litre between 1927 and 1931, with around 720 units built. A continuation series introduced in 2019 saw an additional 12 units roll off the assembly line. All cars were powered by 4.4-liter inline-four engines, offered in both naturally aspirated and supercharged flavors.
The all-motor version came with 110 horsepower on tap, while the supercharged 4 1/2 Litre delivered 175 horsepower. The race-spec versions had significantly more potent mills, rated at 130 and 240 horsepower, respectively. The supercharged 4 1/2 Litre is also known as the Blower Bentley.
A quick check of the license plate reveals that this barn find is a 1928-model-year car and confirms that it was painted black from the factory. It's unclear if the paint is original, though. Its past is also a mystery, but I can tell you a few things about the car's future. If this vehicle makes it on the auction block , it will probably sell for a six-figure sum as is.
Moreover, this Bentley will most likely morph into a million-dollar classic with a full restoration. The 4 1/2 Litre is one of the most desirable Bentleys ever produced, and several examples have changed hands for million-dollar sums in recent years.
The supercharged models tend to fetch between $2 and $8 million depending on condition and specs, but a few naturally aspirated examples also changed hands for over $1 million. The big question is, will this Bentley be rescued before it becomes a rust bucket?
By the way, this Bentley is a Sports Tourer with coachwork by Vanden Plas . Only 204 units were bodied by this builder, and only 148 were four-seat versions like this one. Records show that over 50 were put together in 1928. Check it out in the video below.
